turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (NURSE): Morning. I'll grab a few numbers before the doctor comes through. Arm out for me, thanks.
[SEG0002] person_2 (PATIENT): Of course. Thank you for fitting me in today.
[SEG0003] person_1 (NURSE): Blood pressure is one twenty-eight over 78. Pulse is 96. Oxygen sat is 99 percent. Temp is 36.7.
[SEG0004] person_3 (DOCTOR): Hello. I'm Dr Shah. You look a bit wound up, which is completely understandable. Who's with us on the phone?
[SEG0005] person_2 (PATIENT): Good morning, doctor. That is my partner, Alex. I asked them to phone in, as they were speaking with me when it happened.
[SEG0006] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Hi. I can hear you both. I'll add bits if he skips them.
[SEG0007] person_3 (DOCTOR): Lovely. What brought you in today?
[SEG0008] person_2 (PATIENT): I came because of a sudden tightness in my chest on the train. I thought I was having a heart attack.
[SEG0009] person_3 (DOCTOR): That sounds really frightening. Tell me how it unfolded.

[SEG0010] person_2 (PATIENT): It was three days ago, umm, on the morning train into the city. I was standing, and the tightness came across my chest all at once. Then there was a wave of fear, and I started shaking.
[SEG0011] person_3 (DOCTOR): How long did it last?
[SEG0012] person_2 (PATIENT): A few minutes. Err, I did not time it precisely. Perhaps ten. I stepped off at the next station and sat down.

[SEG0013] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): He rang me from the platform. He could hardly get a sentence out. The shaking was still going, and he kept saying his chest was tight. It eased while we talked, over a few minutes.
[SEG0014] person_3 (DOCTOR): And right now, what's still with you?

[SEG0015] person_2 (PATIENT): The tightness, the shaking and the fright have all passed. Since then I feel like a wet rag. On the platform my feet feel dead. Well, they felt dead, and they are normal again now.
[SEG0016] person_2 (PATIENT): My shoulders ache. I think I've overdone it with the extra shifts. The office is so loud I can't hear myself think, but that is only the building works.
[SEG0017] person_3 (DOCTOR): Right. So the feet came good once you were sitting. Are the shoulders a sharp pain or more an ache?
[SEG0018] person_2 (PATIENT): An ache, doctor. Tired muscle, I would say. Not sharp.
[SEG0019] person_3 (DOCTOR): Anything going on in the throat, separate from the train?
[SEG0020] person_2 (PATIENT): Yes. I have had a frog in my throat for a while. Umm, I cannot date it. Last winter, or the one before.
[SEG0021] person_3 (DOCTOR): No worries, we won't force a date. During the episode, were you short of breath?
[SEG0022] person_2 (PATIENT): Yes. I could not fill my lungs properly. It passed as the tightness passed.
[SEG0023] person_3 (DOCTOR): Was your heart racing, or pounding?
[SEG0024] person_2 (PATIENT): Pounding, yes. Quite hard.
[SEG0025] person_3 (DOCTOR): Any sweating?
[SEG0026] person_2 (PATIENT): A cold sweat, yes.
[SEG0027] person_3 (DOCTOR): Did you black out at any point?
[SEG0028] person_2 (PATIENT): No. I stayed conscious throughout.
[SEG0029] person_3 (DOCTOR): Did the tightness move into your arm or your jaw?
[SEG0030] person_2 (PATIENT): No. It remained across the chest.
[SEG0031] person_3 (DOCTOR): Nausea, or any vomiting?
[SEG0032] person_2 (PATIENT): No, neither.
[SEG0033] person_3 (DOCTOR): On ordinary days, any cough, wheeze, or breathlessness?
[SEG0034] person_2 (PATIENT): No. My breathing is fine otherwise.
[SEG0035] person_3 (DOCTOR): And the stomach, any ongoing trouble?
[SEG0036] person_2 (PATIENT): No, nothing there.
[SEG0037] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): He was very pale on the video. I don't think he could see it. The colour came back after the shaking stopped.
[SEG0038] person_2 (PATIENT): I will accept that. I did not see my own face.
[SEG0039] person_3 (DOCTOR): Are you on any medicines? Anything from the chemist, inhalers, vitamins?
[SEG0040] person_2 (PATIENT): No. I take nothing at all. A colleague once mentioned propranalol, but I have never taken it. I do not use drugs of any kind.
[SEG0041] person_3 (DOCTOR): Ok. Any old test results floating around, even vague ones?
[SEG0042] person_2 (PATIENT): A couple of years ago the GP did cholesterol bloods, and they said it was borderline. I was not given a figure.
[SEG0043] person_3 (DOCTOR): Then we won't invent one. Tell me about your family, anyone who comes to mind.

[SEG0044] person_2 (PATIENT): My father had diabetes in his fifties, and my mother did not. My older sister has pressure, but no sugar. My grandfather on my father's side had a heart attack in his sixties, and my brother is perfectly well.
[SEG0045] person_3 (DOCTOR): What does a normal week look like for you? Work, meals, exercise, a drink.

[SEG0046] person_2 (PATIENT): I am a records clerk at the council, and I work about 45 hours a week with the extra shifts. I skip breakfast and I eat rather a lot of takeaway. Uh, I do not really exercise, apart from a walk on Sunday. I have two or three beers on a Friday night, and I have never smoked.
[SEG0047] person_3 (DOCTOR): Mm. Let me listen. Heart sounds are normal, no murmur. Chest is clear. The pulse is regular. No swelling at the ankles.

[SEG0048] person_3 (DOCTOR): I think this was most likely a panic attack, the first one you've had. It came with fear and shaking, it settled, and the examination is reassuring. I still can't properly rule out a heart rhythm problem until we've got a tracing.

[SEG0049] person_3 (DOCTOR): I'd like an ECG today, before you leave. And I'll teach you a breathing pattern. Breathe in for four, hold for four, out for six. Practise that once a day, and if the tightness starts again, sit down and do it.
[SEG0050] person_1 (NURSE): I can take you for the ECG in the side room straight after. The machine is free.
[SEG0051] person_2 (PATIENT): Thank you. I will practise. When would you like me to return?

[SEG0052] person_3 (DOCTOR): Come back in one week and we'll look at the ECG together. If the pain becomes crushing, or you collapse, or it carries on beyond about ten minutes, call an ambulance. Don't wait on the appointment.
[SEG0053] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): I'll be around if it happens again. Thanks for having me on the line.
[SEG0054] person_2 (PATIENT): I am very grateful. We shall see you in a week.

spec.situation: Young adult after a first episode of sudden chest tightness, shaking and fear on a train; thinks it was a heart attack; no drugs; partner phones in details; doctor orders ECG, teaches breathing.

traps.happens: The patient describes things in colourful or sentence-like speech ('I've overdone it', 'I can't hear myself think', 'a frog in my throat', 'my feet feel dead', 'I feel like a wet rag').
traps.label_rule: Every symptom name is a short clinical noun phrase of 1 to 5 words ('voice fatigue', 'numbness in both feet', 'tiredness'), never a full sentence, never starting with I/we/my. Pure idioms that are not symptoms ('I can't hear myself think' said about classroom noise) are NOT symptoms. The patient's own words stay in the cited turn, not in the name.

traps.happens: In ONE long answer the patient lists several relatives and their conditions ('my father had diabetes in his fifties, mother did not, another sister has pressure but no sugar'), and in another long answer their job, hours, diet, exercise and alcohol.
traps.label_rule: Every relative with a stated condition is a separate family_history entry (relative, condition). Relatives said NOT to have a condition are not family_history entries. Occupation, hours, diet, exercise and alcohol/tobacco each become social_history entries as said (no inventions). Nothing from the doctor's questions is a fact.

features: test_result_recalled: the patient reports an old test or result ('they said it was borderline'); recorded as reported history/investigation only as far as said, not as a confirmed value.
vague_dates: the patient cannot date things ('since Diwali or after', 'last winter, or the one before'); no invented date; a date_uncertain item.

Palpitations were described specifically as the heart pounding quite hard.

Past investigation result: cholesterol bloods a couple of years ago were said to be borderline, figure unknown.
Family history negative details: mother did not have diabetes, and brother is well.
Physical exam finding: chest is clear.
Nurse stated the ECG could be done immediately in the side room straight after because the machine was free.
Planned follow-up purpose: return in one week to review the ECG together.
